model_output.verdict: Executive assistant work for founders and a CEO comes through, with questions about the time between roles.
write_up: Your resume tells a coherent story: you moved from an administrative assistant role at Parkway Logistics to supporting its CEO, and now support founders independently. A recruiter can see the work and would likely move you forward with a few questions.

The line about supporting three founders is a good model: it names who you support, how many, and the work you handle. The dates also leave time between Parkway Logistics and your freelance role unaccounted for, so a recruiter may wonder what you were doing then.

Start with that time between roles, then add a little more about the investor meetings and your work with the CEO's department heads. You don't need to add a number to every line; naming what you handled will do a lot of the work.

cards.line: The Parkway Logistics role ended June 2023, and freelance work began February 2025.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what you were doing between these roles. If you were caring for someone, took a career break, studied, volunteered, or did freelance work, you can name it honestly.
cards.question: What were you doing between the Parkway Logistics role and your freelance work?

cards.line: - Support three founders at early-stage companies with calendar, travel, and inbox management
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives a recruiter a concrete picture of your day-to-day responsibilities and the people counting on you.

cards.line: - Coordinate investor meeting logistics across time zones
cards.cannot_tell: Investor meetings are useful context, but logistics can cover a lot. A recruiter can't tell which parts of the meetings you coordinate.
cards.example: Coordinate investor meeting logistics across time zones, including [what you coordinate]
cards.question: Which parts of the investor meetings do you coordinate?

cards.where: Executive Assistant to the CEO, line 2
cards.line: - Prepared materials for quarterly board meetings
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the board meeting schedule, but not what you prepared. Name the materials so they can see your part in the meetings.
cards.question: What materials did you prepare for the board meetings?

cards.where: Executive Assistant to the CEO, line 4
cards.line: - Served as the point of contact between the CEO and department heads
cards.cannot_tell: Being the point of contact doesn't say what you handled between the CEO and department heads. What came through you?
cards.example: Served as the point of contact between the CEO and department heads for [what you handled]
cards.question: What did you handle between the CEO and department heads?

cards.line: - Supported the operations team with scheduling and filing
cards.cannot_tell: This names the tasks, but leaves a recruiter guessing what you scheduled and filed for operations.
cards.example: Supported the operations team by scheduling [what you scheduled] and filing [what you filed]
cards.question: What did you schedule and file for the operations team?

fit.why: Your current work supports three founders, following a role supporting the CEO at Parkway Logistics.
fit.level: Experienced executive assistant, supporting founders and a CEO
fit.note: Your experience points toward executive assistant work with senior leaders or founders. Your freelance work also shows that you can support multiple clients.
